items.stem: Which one of the following statements about topographical maps and the Survey of India indexing is NOT correct?
items.answer: A 1:250,000 sheet covers 15' by 15'.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. It covers 1° by 1°; a 1:50,000 sheet covers 15' by 15'.
options: Topographical maps show relief, drainage, vegetation, settlements, transport and land use.
A 1:250,000 sheet covers 15' by 15'.
Topographical maps are prepared by the Survey of India.
A 1:250,000 sheet is divided into 16 sheets on 1:50,000 scale, numbered 1 to 16, such as 53A/1.

items.stem: On a topographical map with a contour interval of 50 m, a road crosses 8 contour intervals (from 100 m to 500 m) over a horizontal distance of 2,000 m. What is its gradient?
items.answer: 1 in 5
items.markingKey: (c) Vertical interval = 8 × 50 = 400 m; gradient = VI ÷ HE = 400 ÷ 2,000 = 1 in 5.
options: 1 in 10
1 in 40
1 in 5
1 in 2

items.stem: What is meant by 'topographical map' in the context of topographical maps and the Survey of India indexing?
items.answer: A large-scale map prepared by precise survey showing natural and man-made features of an area.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: topographical map correctly explained as a large-scale map prepared by precise survey showing natural and man-made features of an area.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about contours, methods of depicting relief and drawing cross-sections:
I. In a convex slope, contours are close at the top and wide apart at the bottom.
II. Contours never cross each other except in the case of an overhanging cliff.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: That is a concave slope; a convex slope has wide spacing at the top and close spacing at the bottom. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: The following statement about topographical maps and the Survey of India indexing is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "A 1:50,000 sheet is divided into sixteen 1:25,000 sheets."
items.answer: It is divided into four 1:25,000 sheets (NE, NW, SE, SW).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It is divided into four 1:25,000 sheets (NE, NW, SE, SW).); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about contours, methods of depicting relief and drawing cross-sections is correct?
items.answer: When contours are evenly spaced, the slope is uniform.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: They do not cross except at an overhanging cliff. That is a concave slope; a convex slope has wide spacing at the top and close spacing at the bottom. Closely spaced contours indicate a steep slope.
options: Contours often cross each other.
Closely spaced contours indicate a gentle slope.
When contours are evenly spaced, the slope is uniform.
In a convex slope, contours are close at the top and wide apart at the bottom.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to identification of landforms and interpretation of topographical maps.
(a) Give a reason for the following: Roads and railways follow valleys in hilly areas. (1)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "Contours of a plateau are widely spaced at the margins." (2)
items.answer: (a) Valleys offer gentle gradients and easier construction. (b) They are closely spaced at the margins and widely spaced on top.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (a) 1 for the reason – valleys offer gentle gradients and easier construction. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – They are closely spaced at the margins and widely spaced on top. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.answer: Contours – lines joining points of equal height
items.markingKey: (b) Contours – lines joining points of equal height. Layer tints – colours for different height zones; Hachures – short lines along the direction of slope; Spot height – dot with exact height of a point are the correct pairs for the others.
options: Layer tints – short lines along the direction of slope
Contours – lines joining points of equal height
Spot height – colours for different height zones
Hachures – dot with exact height of a point

items.stem: What is meant by 'plateau' in the context of identification of landforms and interpretation of topographical maps?
items.answer: An extensive elevated flat area, shown by contours closely spaced at the margins and widely spaced in the middle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: plateau correctly explained as an extensive elevated flat area, shown by contours closely spaced at the margins and widely spaced in the middle.

items.stem: The following statement about identification of landforms and interpretation of topographical maps is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Contours of a plateau are widely spaced at the margins."
items.answer: They are closely spaced at the margins and widely spaced on top.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (They are closely spaced at the margins and widely spaced on top.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on topographical maps and the Survey of India indexing and answer the questions that follow.
"Conventional signs make topographical maps easy to read without lengthy descriptions. Topographical maps show relief, drainage, vegetation, settlements, transport and land use. Topographical maps are prepared by the Survey of India."
(i) A topographical sheet on 1:250,000 scale covers: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'India and Adjacent Countries Series' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Topographical maps are numbered by a reference system. (1)
items.answer: (i) 1° latitude by 1° longitude (ii) The Survey of India series in which 4° by 4° sheets are numbered and divided into smaller sheets. (iii) A sheet can be located quickly from its number, such as 53A/1.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) 1° latitude by 1° longitude (ii) The Survey of India series in which 4° by 4° sheets are numbered and divided into smaller sheets. (iii) A sheet can be located quickly from its number, such as 53A/1.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
items.answer: Layer tints – shading of slopes assuming light from the north-west

options: Contours – lines joining points of equal height

Layer tints – shading of slopes assuming light from the north-west

items.stem: How many Survey of India sheets on the scale of 1:50,000 (15′ × 15′) are there in one sheet of 1:1,000,000 (4° × 4°)?
items.markingKey: (b) Divide the extents: 1:1,000,000 (4° × 4°) ÷ 1:50,000 (15′ × 15′) gives 256 sheets, designated number/letter/number such as 53A/1.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about identification of landforms and interpretation of topographical maps is correct?
items.answer: Transport routes generally follow gentle slopes and avoid steep relief.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: They are closely spaced at the margins and widely spaced on top. A spur's V points to lower ground; a valley's V points to higher ground. Roads usually follow gentle slopes and valleys.
options: Contours of a plateau are widely spaced at the margins.
Roads usually run across the steepest slopes.
Transport routes generally follow gentle slopes and avoid steep relief.
A spur is shown by V-shaped contours pointing towards higher ground.

items.stem:
Statement: Closely spaced contours show a steep slope.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: The land rises a large height over a short horizontal distance.
items.markingKey: (c) The land rises a large height over a short horizontal distance.
options: They show many features in little space and make the map readable to all users.
They give exact heights and show the shape and slope of land.
The land rises a large height over a short horizontal distance.
A point cannot have two different heights, except under an overhanging cliff.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"A 1:250,000 sheet is divided into 16 sheets on 1:50,000 scale, numbered 1 to 16, such as 53A/1. Conventional signs make topographical maps easy to read without lengthy descriptions. Topographical maps are prepared by the Survey of India. Topographical maps show relief, drainage, vegetation, settlements, transport and land use."
(i) Explain the term 'conventional signs', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Topographical maps use conventional signs and colours. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "A 1:50,000 sheet is divided into sixteen 1:25,000 sheets." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) Standard symbols and colours used on topographical maps to show features. (ii) They show many features in little space and make the map readable to all users. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is divided into four 1:25,000 sheets (NE, NW, SE, SW).
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Standard symbols and colours used on topographical maps to show features. (ii) They show many features in little space and make the map readable to all users. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is divided into four 1:25,000 sheets (NE, NW, SE, SW).

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
items.answer: Plateau – concentric contours rising evenly to a summit
